brief.greeting: Good morning. Kernel stacks are getting slimmer while OpenAI’s storage is getting faster – a tiny win in a chip‑starved world.

stories.headline: Kernel stacks shrink amid chip shortage
stories.body: **Shrinking the stack:** At the Linux Plumbers Conference, Will Deacon announced a push to reduce kernel stack memory to cope with the global chip shortage.
stories.why: Smaller stacks free RAM on constrained devices, letting you pack more work into the same silicon.

stories.headline: OpenAI speeds reads twelvefold for a billion users
stories.body: **Twelve‑times the speed:** OpenAI’s Habitat now serves over 1 billion ChatGPT users with reads 12× faster, using multi‑tenancy, global caching, and Azure Cosmos DB.
stories.why: Lower latency means your prompts feel instant, even at massive scale.

stories.headline: LitPivot maps literature for idea generation
stories.body: **Contextual research assistant:** Hugging Face launched LitPivot, a tool that dynamically places your research ideas within the evolving literature landscape.
stories.why: Helps you spot gaps and avoid reinventing the wheel before you start coding.

quick_hits.text: **Open‑source AI coworker:** Anil‑matcha/open‑duet offers self‑hosted Claude‑style agents with memory and approval gates.
**C++ media server:** ZLMediaKit provides a full‑stack WebRTC/RTMP/HTTP streaming framework.
**MOSS‑Image popularity:** Hugging Face’s image model hit 1.6 M downloads, 405 likes.
**DIY coil winder:** A hackathon project automates flip‑dot matrix winding.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow – keep those kernels lean.

highlights.title: [$] Seeking smaller kernel stacks
highlights.summary: At the 2026 Linux Plumbers Conference, Will Deacon highlighted renewed efforts to shrink kernel stack memory amid a global chip shortage.
highlights.detail: Kernel stacks historically consume a fixed amount of memory per thread; reducing their size could lower overall RAM pressure for embedded and cloud workloads. The discussion reflects broader industry moves to optimize memory footprints.

highlights.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)
highlights.summary: OpenAI scaled Habitat to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users, achieving 12× faster reads via multi‑tenancy, global caching, and Azure Cosmos DB.
highlights.detail: The redesign introduced reliable multi‑tenant isolation and a distributed cache that reduces latency across regions. Azure Cosmos DB provides globally consistent storage, allowing the system to handle peak traffic spikes without degradation. This architecture builds on earlier OpenAI storage layers but adds tighter latency guarantees.

highlights.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
highlights.summary: OpenAI added offline environments and high‑compute red‑team testing to tighten containment for frontier model training and evaluation.
highlights.detail: The new workflow isolates training clusters from external networks and runs adversarial attacks on dedicated high‑performance hardware, reducing risk of data leakage. These measures complement existing sandboxing and monitoring tools, aiming to prevent unintended model behavior before deployment.

highlights.title: Security
highlights.summary: Anthropic posted a Security page but provided no additional information.
highlights.detail: The brief entry appears on Anthropic's site without details on policies, audits, or technical safeguards, offering no actionable insight for readers.

items.title: LitPivot: Developing research ideas through dynamic contextualization within the literature landscape
items.summary: Hugging Face introduced LitPivot, a tool that dynamically contextualizes research ideas within the literature landscape.
items.detail: LitPivot lets users explore related papers, track emerging topics, and visualize connections in real time, aiming to accelerate hypothesis generation. It integrates with existing Hugging Face datasets and search APIs, positioning itself as a research assistance platform.

items.title: Model: Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image
items.summary: The MOSS-Image model on Hugging Face has been downloaded 1,606,363 times and received 405 likes.
items.detail: MOSS-Image is a vision model that gained rapid community adoption, reflected in its high download count. The like count indicates positive reception among developers, though no performance metrics are provided in the listing.

items.title: Model: InternScience/Sage-A1.5
items.summary: The Sage‑A1.5 text‑generation model on Hugging Face has 924 downloads and 260 likes.
items.detail: Sage‑A1.5 targets general‑purpose text generation and has attracted modest community interest. The download and like figures suggest a niche but engaged user base, pending further benchmark reporting.

items.title: Model: MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash
items.summary: MiniMaxAI released the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash image‑text‑to‑text model, which has received 1,096 downloads and 270 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model is part of the MiniMax series targeting flash‑compatible deployments. It supports converting images and accompanying text into textual output, aiming for low‑latency inference on edge devices.

items.title: [$] The first part of the 7.4 merge window
items.summary: The Linux 7.4 merge window has already integrated 6,753 non‑merge changesets, with a possible extension to a three‑week window.
items.detail: These changes include new kernel features, extensive clean‑ups, and security patches. Extending the window would allow more contributions before the release cut‑off, potentially increasing the feature set of the upcoming kernel.

items.title: Automatic Coil Winder Takes the Tedium out of Actuators
items.summary: A DIY automatic coil winder was built to eliminate the tedious manual winding required for flip‑dot matrix displays.
items.detail: The device automates the placement of wire turns on actuator coils, improving consistency and speed. It is useful for hobbyists constructing custom displays or small‑scale electromechanical projects.

items.title: Hackaday Podcast Episode 392: Microscopes, Drones, and Other DIY Things
items.summary: Hackaday Podcast Episode 392 discusses recent DIY projects, including microscopes, drones, and other small‑scale inventions.
items.detail: Hosts Elliot and Al Williams review the week’s highlights, covering both hardware hacks and cybersecurity topics, offering listeners insights into emerging maker trends.

items.title: Reconstructing the Ancient Chinese Storm of Crows Weapon
items.summary: An article reconstructs the ancient Chinese "Storm of Crows" large crossbow, noting its similarity to Greco‑Roman ballistae.
items.detail: The weapon featured a single massive bolt and was used for siege warfare. The reconstruction sheds light on historical engineering parallels between East Asian and Mediterranean military technologies.

items.title: RepRapMicron Uses Fibre Optics To Print Tiny Benchy in Resin
items.summary: The RepRapMicron µRepRap adds a UV print head that uses fibre optics to cure resin, enabling it to print a miniature version of the standard Benchy model.
items.detail: This micro‑scale 3‑D printer adapts the open‑source RepRap philosophy to the sub‑millimetre regime, combining a tiny mechanical frame with a light‑guided UV source. The fibre‑optic delivery allows precise resin exposure, expanding the range of printable geometries beyond typical filament extrusion. It demonstrates how established desktop printing concepts can be miniaturized for research and hobbyist applications.

items.title: anomalyco/hex
items.summary: hex is a Rust‑based local‑first voice dictation app for macOS that runs speech recognition on‑device and also offers a Linux beta.
items.detail: The tool activates via a configurable shortcut, captures spoken input, and pastes the transcribed text into any active application, keeping data local. Its native Rust implementation aims for low latency and privacy. The Linux beta expands platform coverage beyond macOS.
